title: Resumable delivery & robustness for scheduled customer CSV exports (S3 + webhooks)
text:
Resumable delivery & robustness for scheduled customer CSV exports (S3 + webhooks)

description:
Replace the brittle scheduled CSV export runner with a resumable, tenant-aware delivery system that guarantees at-least-once delivery to S3 and webhook endpoints, provides idempotent manifests for consumer deduplication, enforces per-tenant throttles and data residency, and exposes explicit observability for export lag and delivery failures.

acceptance_criteria:
Scheduled exports can be resumed from the last committed watermark after a service restart without duplicating rows more than once for consumers that follow the idempotent manifest protocol
S3 deliveries use multipart uploads with atomic manifest publish to a per-tenant prefix and are visible in the exports dashboard with start/complete timestamps
Webhook deliveries follow exponential backoff + jitter with per-tenant rate limiting and circuit-breaker after N consecutive 5xx responses, moving payloads to a per-tenant dead-letter queue
Export schema version is recorded in every manifest; consumers can request a historical manifest and the system returns a signed URL for the CSV and a checksum
Export lag and failure rates are shown in a per-tenant dashboard; SLAs are evaluated by the new export_lag_seconds and export_delivery_errors metrics
Integration tests simulate partition loss and confirm resumability across restarts and retry windows

technical_notes:
Design decision: adopt at-least-once delivery with idempotent manifest keys instead of attempting distributed exactly-once across consumers. Exactly-once would require cross-tenant dedupe state and >2x complexity for marginal benefit.
Manifest format: newline-delimited JSON lines describing file_url, checksum, schema_version, export_watermark, row_count, delivery_attempts. Manifest key = tenant_id + export_id + manifest_sequence — consumers should dedupe on export_id + checksum.
S3 pattern: tenant/{tenant_id}/exports/{export_id}/v{schema_version}/{filename}.csv and tenant/{tenant_id}/exports/{export_id}/manifest.json; publish manifest only after successful multipart complete
Webhook semantics: deliver manifest -> then POST with either manifest metadata or signed URL. If webhook responds 2xx, mark delivered; on 4xx mark permanent failure and move to DLQ after logging; on 5xx retry with exponential backoff and jitter up to 6 attempts
Throttling: token-bucket per-tenant in the delivery workers; config driven from tenant profile with defaults and override by Dedicated customers
Data residency: enforce region-scoped S3 bucket selection using tenant.region; scheduled exports for EU tenants must write to eu-exports-prod buckets only
Observability: new Prometheus/Grafana metrics export_lag_seconds (histogram), manifest_publish_duration_seconds, delivery_retries_total{outcome}, dlq_events_total
Runbook link: Confluence - Export Delivery Runbook (internal) - includes steps to replay, purge DLQ, and revoke credentials
Security: manifests signed with KMS key per-region; temporary signed S3 URLs expire in 24 hours by default

rollout_plan:
Feature-flag the new runner per environment. Start with non-production tenants in staging, then enable for 10% of production tenants by tenant_id hashing. Monitor export_lag_seconds and dlq_events_total for 48 hours before expanding. Provide toggle to fall back to legacy exporter for rapid rollback.

testing_plan:
Unit tests for manifest serialization, checksum validation, and idempotency checks
Integration test suite that spins up a minio S3 emulator and a webhook sink; validates end-to-end CSV generation, multipart upload, manifest publish, webhook handshake, retries, and DLQ transitions
Chaos test: kill delivery worker at random points to validate resumability from watermark and manifest sequence
Load test: 500 concurrent tenant exports with variable sizes to validate token-bucket throttling and autoscaling behavior
Compliance test: validate exports for EU tenant write to EU buckets only and verify KMS key usage

comments:
2026-02-19 - Marco Liu: Initial scoping complete. Built prototype that writes manifest after multipart complete. Observed duplicate rows when consumers polled during manifest publish; added sequencing to manifest to mitigate.
2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Reviewed prototype. Requested stronger invariants around manifest atomicity and checksum validation. Also called out need for per-tenant rate limits to avoid noisy neighbors.
2026-03-02 - Arjun Mehta: Ops reviewed runbook. Suggested adding an operator endpoint to replay a manifest given export_id and sequence to ease customer support.
2026-03-07 - QA: Integration tests passing in staging for small exports (<10MB). Found bug where webhook 429s were treated as 4xx; updated classification to retryable with backoff.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Begin canary rollout to 10% production. Monitoring thresholds set: if export_delivery_errors > 0.5% or export_lag_seconds p95 > 600s for 15m, disable feature flag and revert to legacy runner.
